primary_sources: Kent State University shootings, May 4, 1970 (public record)

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from the grounding books' account of the spring of 1970

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the spring of 1970, from the grounding books.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the spring of 1970. In April 1970, President Nixon sent American troops into Cambodia to destroy Vietcong bases, widening a war he had promised to end. Protests broke out on college campuses. On May 4, 1970, Ohio National Guard troops fired on protesters at Kent State University, killing four students.

stem: The Cambodia invasion and the Kent State shootings together best show which of the following about the war by 1970?

options.text: The war had ended and Americans had stopped debating it
options.misconception: Background: the war went on for years after 1970, and the protests show the debate was fiercer than ever.

options.text: The war was shrinking quietly without any public notice at all
options.misconception: Background: the invasion widened the war and the shootings made national news, so nothing about it was quiet.

options.text: Nixon's widening of the war abroad deepened division at home
College students broadly supported the invasion of Cambodia that spring
options.misconception: Students protested the invasion on campuses across the country, so they did not broadly support it.

rationales.A: Background: the war continued until 1973 for American forces, and the protests show the debate was fierce.
rationales.B: Background: the invasion widened the war and the shootings became national news, so the war was not shrinking quietly.
rationales.C: Background: Nixon widened the war into Cambodia, and the killings at Kent State showed the division reaching American campuses.
rationales.D: The passage says protests broke out on college campuses, so students did not broadly support the invasion.
rationales.general:
1. The passage links two events in one spring: troops sent into Cambodia, then gunfire on an Ohio campus.
2. Background: Nixon had promised to end the war, yet he widened it into a new country.
3. The widening set off campus protests, and at Kent State four students were killed by National Guard troops.
4. The war abroad and the division at home therefore fed each other in the same season.
Remember: When a war widens abroad, watch for the division widening at home.
